title: Normalized point-section and ordinary-image models
statement: For a finite-field datum D, a prime ell different from its characteristic, a finite extension E/Q_ell, and the continuous realization family R, define normalized point-section and integral ordinary-image comparison data; no existence is asserted. Reuse the separated finite-type geometry and actual continuous sections. At s=Spec(k), take the actual rational coefficient object. A coefficient-unit model identifies the integral coefficient transport with the regular module by 1->1 on every site object, and identifies its scalar tensor with the continuous regular module by a tensor b -> a phi(b). The point model consists of a fully faithful realization fixed on integral representatives by the recorded coefficient transport and derived extension, a class e in H0(Fib_s(1_s)), and an E-linear H0(Fib_s K)-to-Hom(1_s,K) equivalence fixed by evaluation at e. Normalize e to the actual tensor 1 tensor 1 through pointRationalNormalization and the exact single-complex comparisons; normalize the realized unit through the universal derived tensor counit and the coefficient-unit multiplication. Define the universal right-derived unit on cochain representatives. For every geometric structure map define an integral pushforward transport whose ordinary map is identity on sections and whose derived comparison commutes on every complex with those right-derived units and the exact coefficient-transport factors. Recover the precise product and Roos vertex used by integralImage. Identify that actual integralImage with the completed ringed direct image, requiring its maps to every finite term to be the scalar-reduction adjunction unit followed by the recorded restriction comparison. Include the finite identity pushforward comparison fixed by the actual base-change identity on sections and its right-derived unit. The exact cohomology comparison is the universal localization lift of the termwise homology comparison, with independent source and target localization Hom universes.
